newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Bell proposes phone rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Bell proposes phone rate hike.

text.p: Two of Canada's largest telephone firms filed proposals on Friday with the national regulator to raise local phone rates to bring them more in line with costs.

BCE Inc's Bell Canada unit, which operates in Ontario and Quebec, said it had asked the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) to approve an average increase in local residential rates by C$1.48 a month from January 1, 1998. Actual increases would range up to C$2.10.
Alberta-based TELUS Corp, the nation's third largest telephone company, also proposed raising local rates for residential consumers by C$3 per line starting January 1, 1998.
Canada's regulatory body was also asked to approve a TELUS proposal that customers in Edmonton, Alberta's capital, would see rates increase by C$2 a month starting August 1, 1997.
Bell Canada's proposals included lowering the contribution rate it charges its long-distance competitors to C$0.0062 a minute.
Bell asked Canada's regulatory body to use a 12.75 percent rate of return on common equity as a level to determine the utility service revenue requirement as a price cap.
Bell also said it planned to invest more than C$1.6 billion to continue improving its local network.

Earlier this year Canada's communications regulatory agency approved a C$3 monthly hike in local phone charges starting on January 1, 1998. That followed increases of C$2 in each of the two previous years, designed to reflect more accurately the cost of providing local phone services, which are subsidized by long-distance calls.
Earlier this week Canada's regulatory body approved an application by Bell to change local business rates and to simplify the different rate levels for those services.
Starting on July 1, business customers will pay a single price of C$45.45 a month for business lines and private branch exchange trunks.
